strengths: DualReg addresses a practically important registration problem with a coherent combination of correspondence filtering, anchor-defined geometric proxies, and robust local refinement. The method works with both handcrafted and learned descriptors without training a new model.

Tables I–III demonstrate a useful accuracy–runtime tradeoff across three benchmarks and two descriptors. On KITTI with FPFH, DualReg achieves 98.20% recall in 0.12 s versus MAC’s 97.48% in 3.91 s, supporting the approximately 32× speedup claim. Reported RMSE, rotation error, and translation error are consistently lower than those of the compared methods.

The ablations provide substantive evidence for coarse filtering and geometric refinement. On 3DLoMatch with FCGF, adding dual-space optimization increases recall from 49.2% to 60.5%; on KITTI with FPFH, it reduces RMSE from 28.22 cm to 12.26 cm.
The manuscript provides equations, filtering pseudocode, hardware information, and many parameter settings. Comparisons include relevant recent methods such as MAC++, TCF, and TurboReg.
weaknesses: The central consensus-set construction is insufficiently specified. Equation (5) requires pairwise consistency but leaves the domain of the quantified correspondence unclear and does not explain how a mutually consistent subset is selected when several exist. Algorithm 1 simply invokes this equation. This missing procedure affects both reproducibility and the claimed efficiency: reducing the number of sampled seeds does not establish the computational cost of constructing each consensus set.

The symmetry rejection rule is not generally valid as stated. A negative determinant of the unconstrained Procrustes solution does not prove that useful correspondences cannot be aligned by a proper rotation. For planar or rank-deficient configurations, proper and improper solutions can attain the same residual; noise can also change the determinant for nearly planar sets. Rejecting the entire set without a rank or residual check can discard valid hypotheses. The average ablation gains support its empirical usefulness but do not resolve this technical limitation.

The experiments do not isolate the main distinction from conventional global registration followed by robust ICP. There is no comparison against TCF or MAC followed by the same robust refinement, nor a controlled comparison between full-cloud and proxy-restricted refinement. Moreover, removing the anchor term leaves 3DLoMatch recall almost unchanged: 41.6% versus 41.6% for FPFH and 60.3% versus 60.5% for FCGF. Thus, the evidence for the necessity of jointly optimizing both correspondence spaces is weaker than the evidence for local geometric refinement.

Runtime and evaluation details leave consequential uncertainty. It is unclear whether timing includes normal estimation, downsampling, and proxy construction, and whether RMSE/RE/TE are averaged over successful registrations only. Different success sets can affect comparisons of conditional errors. The claimed likely speed advantage over TurboReg relies on ratios from different experimental settings rather than a controlled measurement. Repeated-run variability and the selection protocol for dataset-specific parameters are also unreported.

The optimization description needs correction: with transformation-dependent Gaussian weights, Equation (13) is not the fixed robust objective minimized by the stated alternating solver. The updates can instead be understood as an iteratively reweighted procedure for a Welsch-type objective, but that objective and its connection to the updates are not established. Separately, claims of uniformly superior ablation performance overstate Table V: removing refinement improves FCGF 3DLoMatch recall slightly, and patch-wise matching improves FPFH recall.

Overall, the substantial empirical speed and accuracy benefits place this submission near acceptance, but the undefined core subset-selection procedure, overly strong symmetry argument, and incomplete isolation of the dual-space contribution keep the recommendation borderline.

strengths: DualReg addresses a useful problem: efficient rigid registration with noisy correspondences and partial overlap. Combining filtered feature matches with local geometric proxies is well motivated and yields a practical training-free registration backend.

Tables I–III support a strong accuracy–runtime tradeoff across three benchmarks and two descriptors. On KITTI with FPFH, DualReg achieves 98.20% recall in 0.12 s versus MAC's 97.48% in 3.91 s, supporting the approximately 32× speedup claim. On 3DLoMatch with FCGF, it achieves 60.47% recall in 0.16 s versus MAC's 60.13% in 1.97 s. These are valuable results even without uniformly leading recall.

The method reports the lowest RMSE, rotation error, and translation error among the compared methods in all six dataset–descriptor settings. Evaluation includes relevant recent competitors such as MAC++, TCF, and TurboReg.

The ablations provide meaningful evidence for coarse filtering and geometric refinement. In Table V, removing coarse filtering reduces KITTI–FPFH recall from 98.2% to 84.0%; removing dual-space optimization reduces 3DLoMatch–FCGF recall from 60.5% to 49.2%. Hardware, major libraries, and many parameter settings are specified.
weaknesses: The central consensus construction is insufficiently specified. Equation (5) leaves the domain of the universal quantifier over c_k unclear and does not explain how a mutually compatible subset is selected when multiple subsets exist. Algorithm 1 simply invokes this equation. The selection procedure and its computational cost are essential to reproducing the main filtering contribution; reducing the number of possible sampled seeds from O(n³) to O(n) does not establish the complexity of constructing and scoring their consensus sets.

The experiments do not adequately isolate the novelty of dual-space optimization from conventional geometric refinement. The introduction explicitly argues against feature-based initialization followed by robust ICP, but no matched comparison tests that alternative using the same initialization and point access. Likewise, applying the proposed refinement to TCF or MAC would clarify its incremental contribution. Table V's geometry-only variant retains the proposed proxies and nearly matches the full method on 3DLoMatch: 41.6% versus 41.6% recall with FPFH and 60.3% versus 60.5% with FCGF.

The determinant-based rejection rule is not generally justified as stated. For planar or otherwise rank-deficient correspondences, the unconstrained orthogonal Procrustes solution can have determinant −1 even when a proper rotation aligns the points equally well. Rejecting the entire set can therefore discard valid consensus sets. For noisy full-rank data, a negative determinant also does not establish exact mirror symmetry. No degeneracy handling or targeted evaluation addresses this issue.

The optimization formulation needs correction or clarification. Equation (13), with residual-dependent weights from Equation (14), is not the objective directly minimized by repeatedly freezing those weights and solving weighted least squares. The updates are consistent with a Welsch-type robust objective, but that objective and the relationship to the stated energy are not supplied. This appears repairable, yet the current formulation does not substantiate the claimed optimization of Equation (13).

Runtime and evaluation reporting leave material uncertainty. It is unclear whether timings include normal estimation, downsampling, proxy construction, and feature extraction, and whether error averages use all pairs or only successful registrations. The inferred speed advantage over TurboReg relies on cross-paper runtime ratios rather than a matched measurement. Dataset-dependent parameter choices lack a validation protocol or sensitivity study, and randomized sampling results have no repeated-run variability.

Several conclusions exceed the evidence. Table V does not show uniform superiority of the complete method: omitting refinement raises 3DLoMatch–FCGF recall from 60.5% to 60.8%, and patch-wise processing raises FPFH recall from 41.6% to 41.9%. Claims of a 'perfect synergy' or an 'optimal balance' should be moderated. These presentation issues are secondary; the borderline recommendation primarily reflects the balance between substantial reported practical gains and unresolved core algorithm specification, correctness, and contribution-isolation concerns.

strengths: DualReg addresses a practically important problem: accurate rigid registration with low CPU runtime. Combining filtered feature correspondences with local geometric proxies is well motivated, particularly for partial overlap.

Tables I–III demonstrate a strong accuracy–runtime tradeoff across three benchmarks and two descriptors. On KITTI with FPFH, DualReg achieves 98.20% recall versus MAC’s 97.48%, reduces RMSE from 15.57 to 12.26 cm, and reduces runtime from 3.91 to 0.12 seconds, supporting the advertised approximately 32× speedup.

The method reports the lowest RMSE, rotation error, and translation error among the compared methods in all six dataset–descriptor settings. Recall remains competitive, although it is not consistently highest. This combination has value without requiring universal benchmark dominance.

The ablations provide meaningful evidence for coarse filtering and geometric refinement. In Table V, removing coarse filtering reduces KITTI FPFH recall from 98.2% to 84.0%; removing dual-space optimization reduces 3DLoMatch FCGF recall from 60.5% to 49.2%.

The manuscript includes equations, filtering pseudocode, implementation libraries, hardware specifications, and many parameter settings. Comparisons include relevant recent methods such as MAC++, TCF, and TurboReg.
weaknesses: A central algorithmic step is insufficiently specified. Equation (5) does not define the domain of the universally quantified correspondence or explain how a mutually compatible subset is selected when several exist. Algorithm 1 simply refers back to this equation. The selection procedure and its complexity are essential to reproducing both filtering quality and the main efficiency claim; counting O(n) possible seeds instead of O(n³) triples does not characterize the cost of constructing each consensus set.

The symmetry rejection rule has an important degeneracy issue. A negative determinant of the unconstrained Procrustes solution does not establish that valid rigid alignment is impossible: for rank-deficient, especially planar, correspondence sets, an improper and a proper orthogonal transformation can fit equally well. Rejecting the entire set without checking rank or comparing proper-rotation residuals can discard valid correspondences. No targeted evaluation establishes robustness to this case.

The experiments do not isolate the advantage over the straightforward alternative discussed in the introduction: the same coarse registration followed by conventional robust ICP on the full clouds. The geometry-only ablation still uses the proposed proxies. Thus, the experiments support geometric refinement but do not fully establish the distinctive benefit of proxy restriction and joint feature–geometry optimization over an appropriately matched registration-plus-ICP baseline.

The optimization formulation needs clarification. With the residual-dependent weights in Equation (14) substituted into Equation (13), the objective contains terms r² exp(−r²/(2σ²)), which approach zero for arbitrarily large residuals. The stated frozen-weight SVD iterations are instead consistent with an iteratively reweighted solver for a Welsch-type robust objective. This distinction does not invalidate the implementation, but the manuscript does not correctly connect the stated objective and solver.

Efficiency and reproducibility evidence have gaps. Runtime accounting does not clearly specify whether normal estimation, downsampling, feature extraction, and proxy construction are included. The claimed likely speed advantage over TurboReg is inferred from ratios across separate experiments rather than a matched measurement. Dataset-specific parameter choices, particularly α, lack a tuning protocol or sensitivity analysis, and randomized results have no reported variation.

Several claims exceed the evidence. Table V shows higher 3DLoMatch FCGF recall without refinement (60.8% versus 60.5%) and higher FPFH recall with patch-wise processing (41.9% versus 41.6%), contradicting the assertion that the full method is uniformly superior. These are correctable presentation issues. Overall, the convincing empirical tradeoff places the work near acceptance, but the unresolved consensus construction, degeneracy handling, and attribution of gains keep my assessment borderline.

strengths: DualReg addresses a practically important registration problem with a coherent combination of correspondence filtering, anchor-centered geometric proxies, and robust refinement. The contribution has value as an efficient, training-free registration pipeline.

Table 1 demonstrates a strong CPU speed–accuracy tradeoff across three benchmarks and two descriptors. On KITTI with FPFH, DualReg achieves 98.20% recall and 12.26 cm RMSE in 0.12 s, versus MAC’s 97.48%, 15.57 cm, and 3.91 s. Its reported RMSE, rotation error, and translation error are lowest across all six dataset–descriptor settings.

The ablations provide meaningful evidence for geometric refinement. On 3DLoMatch with FCGF, adding dual-space optimization raises recall from 49.2% to 60.9% and reduces RMSE from 11.16 to 7.81 cm. KITTI also shows substantial alignment-error reductions.
The supplement supplies implementation parameters, runtime breakdowns, normal-estimation comparisons, and parameter sensitivity experiments. Explicitly distinguishing CPU and GPU timings is helpful.
weaknesses: The central filtering operation is insufficiently specified. Equation (5) leaves the domain of the universal quantifier unclear and does not explain how the pairwise-consistent subset is selected when multiple incompatible candidates exist. Algorithm 1 simply calls this equation. The missing selection procedure affects both reproducibility and the claimed efficiency; reducing the number of possible seeds from O(n³) to O(n) does not establish the complexity of constructing each consensus set.

The reflection rejection rule in Supplement A is not generally valid as stated. A negative determinant of the unconstrained orthogonal fit does not establish exact planar symmetry for noisy correspondences. For rank-deficient, especially planar, configurations, an improper and a proper transformation can fit equally well, so rejecting the entire set based on the SVD determinant can discard valid matches. No degeneracy handling or targeted evaluation is provided.

The experiments do not isolate the advantage over a strong conventional coarse-to-fine pipeline. Comparisons against the same initialization followed by full-cloud robust ICP, and against MAC or TCF followed by comparable refinement, are missing. The anchor-removal ablation still retains the proposed geometric proxies. Consequently, the results establish the utility of refinement more clearly than the distinctive benefit of the proposed dual-space formulation; its anchor contribution is also small on 3DLoMatch.

The evaluation protocol leaves important interpretation gaps. The supplement uses rotation/translation thresholds for indoor recall rather than the customary 3DMatch alignment-RMSE criterion, without reporting the customary metric alongside it. It also does not clearly define RMSE or state whether errors are averaged over successful registrations only. No repeated-run variability is reported despite randomized sampling and several sub-percentage-point recall differences.

Some technical and efficiency claims exceed the evidence. Equations (10)–(11) make weights transformation-dependent, whereas the solver freezes them; this is consistent with a Welsch-style reweighting scheme but does not directly minimize the written objective after substituting those weights. Timing coverage for normal estimation and preprocessing is unclear, and the suggested CPU advantage over TurboReg is inferred across different experimental environments rather than measured directly.

strengths: The method addresses a practically important problem: accurate rigid registration with low CPU runtime. Its combination of correspondence filtering, anchor-centered geometric proxies, and robust refinement is coherent and potentially useful.

Table 1 demonstrates a strong accuracy–runtime tradeoff across indoor, low-overlap, and outdoor benchmarks using both FPFH and FCGF. On KITTI with FPFH, DualReg achieves 98.20% recall in 0.12 s versus MAC's 97.48% in 3.91 s, supporting the advertised approximately 32× speedup in that setting. Reported RMSE, rotation error, and translation error improve across all six dataset–descriptor combinations.

The ablations provide meaningful support for the pipeline. In Table 2, removing dual-space optimization reduces 3DLoMatch FCGF recall from 60.9% to 49.2%; on KITTI FCGF, refinement reduces RMSE from 27.52 cm to 10.78 cm while preserving recall.

The supplementary material provides runtime breakdowns, parameter sensitivity experiments, and tests of normal-estimation settings. These strengthen the empirical support beyond the main benchmark table. Hardware and CPU/GPU timing distinctions are explicitly disclosed.
weaknesses: A central filtering operation is insufficiently specified. Equation (5) requires a pairwise-consistent subset but does not define the domain of the universally quantified correspondence or explain how the subset is selected when multiple incompatible subsets exist. Algorithm 1 merely refers back to this equation. Whether this uses a greedy construction, an exhaustive compatibility test, or clique search materially affects both results and computational cost. Consequently, the claimed reduction from O(n³) to O(n) candidate samples does not establish the computational complexity of the filtering algorithm.

The evaluation does not adequately isolate the main claimed advance over coarse registration followed by local refinement. Table 1 compares the complete refined pipeline with correspondence-based estimators, but does not include those estimators followed by a matched robust ICP refinement. Table 2 compares patch-wise versus aggregated proxy matching, but neither tests refinement on the full clouds. Thus, the evidence does not establish how much improvement specifically comes from proxy construction and dual-space coupling rather than adding geometric refinement. The indoor anchor ablation is particularly modest: 3DLoMatch FPFH recall changes from 41.6% without anchors to 41.7% with them, with nearly identical RMSE.

The symmetry rejection rule is not generally valid as stated. Supplementary Section A discards an entire consensus set whenever unconstrained orthogonal Procrustes returns determinant −1. For rank-deficient, particularly planar, correspondences, proper and improper orthogonal solutions can fit equally well, so this determinant alone does not establish that rigid alignment is impossible. No rank or degeneracy handling is specified. This is relevant to registration of planar indoor surfaces, although the aggregate experiments do demonstrate that the implemented method often works.

The robust optimization formulation needs clarification. Equation (10), with transformation-dependent Gaussian weights from Equation (11), is not the objective minimized by repeatedly freezing those weights and solving weighted least squares. The updates can instead be interpreted through a Welsch robust objective, but that objective and its connection to the solver are not derived. This is a correctable mathematical formulation issue rather than evidence that the implemented updates are ineffective.

Some empirical claims exceed the supporting evidence. The inferred CPU advantage over TurboReg combines speed ratios from different experimental setups rather than a controlled comparison. Table 4 also does not establish whether normal estimation and proxy preprocessing are included in the reported times. Randomized runs lack reported variability, making small recall differences difficult to assess; for example, KITTI FPFH recall differs from MAC++ by only 0.18 percentage points.

Overall, the substantial benchmark results and useful CPU tradeoff bring this submission close to acceptance. However, the missing specification of the core consensus construction and the absence of controls that isolate the proposed refinement contribution leave consequential reproducibility and attribution concerns. These concerns balance the demonstrated merits and support a borderline recommendation.

strengths: DualReg provides a useful registration pipeline combining fast correspondence filtering, anchor-centered geometric proxies, and robust joint refinement. The contribution is primarily an effective integration of established ideas, with clear practical relevance to CPU-based registration.

Table 1 supports a strong accuracy–runtime tradeoff across indoor, low-overlap, and outdoor benchmarks with both FPFH and FCGF. On KITTI/FPFH, DualReg achieves 98.20% recall in 0.12 s versus MAC's 97.48% in 3.91 s, supporting the approximately 32× speedup claim in that setting. It also reports the lowest RMSE, rotation error, and translation error across all six configurations.

The ablations substantiate the importance of geometric refinement. On 3DLoMatch/FCGF, adding dual-space optimization increases recall from 49.2% to 60.9% and reduces RMSE from 11.16 to 7.81 cm. On KITTI/FCGF, it reduces RMSE from 27.52 to 10.78 cm while preserving recall.

The supplementary material strengthens the empirical support through runtime breakdowns, normal-estimation comparisons, and parameter sensitivity experiments. Together with the breadth of baselines, these results favor weak acceptance despite the methodological and evaluation reservations below.
weaknesses: The core consensus construction is insufficiently specified. Equation (5) leaves the domain of the universally quantified correspondence unclear and does not explain how the pairwise-consistent subset is selected when candidates conflict; Algorithm 1 merely references this equation. Different selection procedures could materially change both accuracy and runtime. The reduction in the number of possible samples from O(n³) to O(n) also does not establish the computational complexity of constructing each consensus set.

The experiments do not fully isolate the advantage over conventional global registration followed by robust ICP. Table 2's 'w/o Anchor' variant still uses the proposed geometric proxies, while 'Whole' means aggregated proxies rather than the original full clouds. A matched refinement baseline would better establish whether proxy restriction and joint anchor optimization explain the improvements. The anchor term contributes little to indoor recall, and weighted sampling yields only very small inlier-ratio gains over random sampling in most Table 3 settings.

The optimization formulation needs mathematical clarification. With weights held fixed, the SVD update is valid. However, substituting the transformation-dependent weights from Equation (11) into Equation (10) does not yield the objective minimized by that update. A robust-loss formulation with an explicitly identified iteratively reweighted surrogate would make the optimization claim precise.

The reflection rejection rule lacks treatment of degenerate geometry. For coplanar correspondences, the orthogonal Procrustes solution can be nonunique, so a negative determinant need not indicate an invalid correspondence set. Rejecting the entire set on this basis could discard valid planar matches; the manuscript does not evaluate this case.

Some empirical claims exceed the reported evidence. Runtime accounting does not clearly establish whether normal estimation and proxy preprocessing are included, and the suggested speed advantage over TurboReg extrapolates across different experimental settings. No repeated-run variability is reported despite randomized sampling, limiting interpretation of small recall differences. The evaluation description also leaves the RMSE definition and error-averaging population unclear. These limitations qualify the claims of superiority without negating the substantial reported accuracy–runtime gains.
